Until you make the unconscious conscious, it will direct your life and you will call it fate.
（除非你将潜意识转化为意识，否则它将主宰你的人生，而你却称之为命运。）
Carl Jung

Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.
（注意力是慷慨最罕见、最纯粹的形式。）
Simone Weil

Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.
(生活只能向后理解，但必须向前生活。)
Søren Kierkegaard

You must be ready to burn yourself in your own fire: how could you become new if you have not first become ashes?
(你必须准备好在自己的烈焰中燃烧自己：若不先化为灰烬，你怎能渴望新生？)
Friedrich Nietzsche

To try always to conquer myself rather than fortune, and to alter my desires rather than the order of the world.
(永远致力于征服自己而非命运，去改变自身的欲望而非世界的秩序。)
René Descartes

Hope is not the conviction that something will turn out well, but the certainty that something makes sense, regardless of how it turns out.
(希望并非笃定某事终将圆满，而是确信某事定有意义，无论其结局如何。)
Vaclav Havel

The value of things is not the time they last, but the intensity with which they occur. That is why there are unforgettable moments, inexplicable things and incomparable people.
(事物的价值不在于其持续的时间，而在于其发生时的强烈程度。正因如此，才有了难忘的瞬间、不可名状的事物与无可比拟的人。)
Fernando Pessoa

Perhaps everything terrible is in its deepest being something helpless that wants help from us.
(或许一切可怕的事物，在其最深处都是某种无助的存在，正渴求着我们的救助。)
Rainer Maria Rilke

Time is a river which sweeps me along, but I am the river; it is a tiger which destroys me, but I am the tiger; it is a fire which consumes me, but I am the fire.
(时间是一条将我卷走其中的河流，但我即是河流；它是一只摧毁我的猛虎，但我即是猛虎；它是一场吞噬我的大火，但我即是大火。)
Jorge Luis Borges

Sometimes, just knowing that there are endless fresh things for me to enjoy is enough to make me glad to be alive.
(有时候，仅仅是知道世间还有无尽的新鲜事物供我欣赏，就足以让我觉得活着真好。)
— Etty Hillesum

Love is the extremely difficult realization that something other than oneself is real.
(爱是一种极其艰难的领悟：认识到除自己之外的事物同样是真实存在的。)
Iris Murdoch

What matters most is how well you walk through the fire.
(最重要的是你如何走过那场烈火。)
Charles Bukowski

Love means to learn to look at yourself the way one looks at distant things, for you are only one thing among many.
(爱意味着学会像凝视遥远事物般审视自己，因为你不过是世间万物中的一员。)
Czesław Miłosz

It may be that when we no longer know what to do, we have come to our real work, and that when we no longer know which way to go, we have begun our real journey.
(也许当我们不再知道该做什么时，我们才真正触及了自身的使命；当我们不再知道该走向何方时，我们才真正踏上了属于自己的旅程。)
—— Wendell Berry

You do not need to leave your room. Remain sitting at your table and listen. Do not even listen, simply wait. Do not even wait, be quiet, still and solitary. The world will freely offer itself to you to be unmasked, it has no choice, it will roll in ecstasy at your feet.
(你无须离开房间。待在桌前倾听；甚至无须倾听，只管等待；甚至无须等待，只需保持彻底的静止与孤独。世界将毫无保留地展露于你，它无法抗拒，并在狂喜中向你席卷而来。)
Franz Kafka

I think we are well advised to keep on nodding terms with the people we used to be.
(我认为，与曾经的自己保持点头之交，是一种明智之举。)
Joan Didion

Knowledge can be communicated, but not wisdom. We can find it, we can live it, we can be carried by it, we can work wonders with it, but we cannot utter it or teach it.
(知识可以被传递，但智慧不能。我们可以去发现智慧，去践行智慧，去被智慧所承载，去凭智慧创造奇迹，但我们无法言说它，也无法传授它。)
Hermann Hesse

If we take eternity to mean not infinite temporal duration but timelessness, then eternal life is that of those who live in the present.
(如果不把永恒理解为时间的无限绵延，而是理解为无时间性，那么活在当下的人便拥有了永恒的生命。)
Ludwig Wittgenstein

One can choose to go back toward safety or forward toward growth. Growth must be chosen again and again; fear must be overcome again and again.
（人可以选择退回安全的舒适区，或是向前迈向成长。成长需要被一次又一次地选择，恐惧也需要被一次又一次地克服。）
Abraham Maslow

Perhaps all the dragons in our lives are princesses who are only waiting to see us act, just once, with beauty and courage.
(也许我们生命中的所有巨龙，都不过是公主，她们只是在等待我们哪怕一次，以美好与勇气去行动。)
— Rainer Maria Rilke

Ultimately, we have just one moral duty: to reclaim large areas of peace in ourselves, more and more peace, and to reflect it toward others.
（归根结底，我们只有一项道德责任：在自己内心重新开垦出一片又一片的宁静，越来越多的宁静，并将这份宁静映照给他人。）
Etty Hillesum（埃蒂·希勒苏姆）

There are years that ask questions and years that answer.
（有些年头提出问题，有些年头给出答案。）
Zora Neale Hurston

Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.
（注意力是最稀有、最纯粹的慷慨。）
Simone Weil
